decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 9-1. Dissenting: Jeffrey M. Lacker.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in July suggests that economic activity is expanding at a moderate pace.”

changes.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment have been increasing at solid rates in recent months, and the housing sector has improved further; however, net exports have been soft.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending and business fixed investment have been increasing moderately, and the housing sector has improved further; however, net exports have been so…”

changes.quote: The pace of job gains slowed and the unemployment rate held steady.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Nonetheless, labor market indicators, on balance, show that underutilization of labor resources has diminished since early this year.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “On balance, labor market indicators show that underutilization of labor resources has diminished since early this year.”

changes.quote: The labor market continued to improve, with solid job gains and declining unemployment.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation moved slightly lower; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Market-based measures of inflation compensation moved lower; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.”

tone_quotes.quote: In determining whether it will be appropriate to raise the target range at its next meeting, the Committee will assess progress--both realized and expected--toward its objectives of maximum employment and 2 percent inflation.

The Committee anticipates that it will be appropriate to raise the target range for the federal funds rate when it has seen some further improvement in the labor market and is reasonably confident that inflation will move back to its 2 percent objective over the medium term.

To support continued progress toward maximum employment and price stability, the Committee today reaffirmed its view that the current 0 to 1/4 percent target range for the federal funds rate remains appropriate.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.04% APR costs about $50.17 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.1% and moved +5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.82% would rise by about $8.56 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5%, and employers added an average of 189k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 0% over the past year (September 2015); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +8 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.23% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 85%, cut 6%, hike 9%.
